title: Encounter contract violations
prompt: The encounters feed has a contract, and the data team wants every visit that breaks it, with the first rule it breaks. Write `solve(encounters)` so it returns those visits.
rules: Check in this order and report the first rule broken: `codes_count` (`diagnosis_codes` has 1 to 3 codes; a missing list breaks it), `times_in_order` (both times present and `end_time` after `start_time`).

Then `vitals_match_class` (a `telehealth` visit has no `vitals`, any other visit has them; a missing class breaks it), then `vitals_complete` (when `vitals` is present, all four readings are present).
A rule that can't be checked because a value is missing counts as broken. Return `encounter_id`, `encounter_class` and `broken`, in that order, only for visits that break a rule. Keep duplicate rows.
hints: `F.size("diagnosis_codes")` counts the codes. Struct fields read as `F.col("vitals.heart_rate")`.
Write each rule true for a good visit and wrap it in `F.coalesce(rule, F.lit(False))`. Then a `F.when` chain on `~rule` picks the first rule broken, and is NULL for a good visit.
For the class rule, `F.when(telehealth, ...).otherwise(...)` sends a missing class to `otherwise`. The rule says a missing class breaks it, so make sure it does.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F


def solve(encounters):
    # Visits that break the contract, with the first rule broken.
    return encounters
explanation: Write the four rules as conditions true for a good visit, make each NULL-safe with `F.coalesce(rule, F.lit(False))`, and label with a `F.when` chain: `F.when(~codes_ok, "codes_count").when(~times_ok, "times_in_order")...`. With no `otherwise`, a good visit gets NULL, so `select("encounter_id", "encounter_class", broken.alias("broken"))` followed by `filter(F.col("broken").isNotNull())` keeps only the violations. `F.size("diagnosis_codes").between(1, 3)` (both ends included, like `>= 1` and `<= 3`) handles an empty list (size 0) and too many codes; a missing list makes it NULL or -1, which breaks either way. Equal start and end times break `times_in_order`, because the end must come after the start. For the class rule, `(telehealth & no_vitals) | (~telehealth & has_vitals)` is NULL for a missing class, and `coalesce` breaks it. `vitals_complete` must pass when there are no vitals at all: that case belongs to the class rule.
